SET UP ONCE. CONNECT FROM IPHONE.

Start with your own Mac.

One iPhone app connects to your Mac’s built-in service. No Mac Companion account or Mac helper installation.

  1. 01

    Enable Screen Sharing

    On the Mac, open System Settings → General → Sharing. Enable Screen Sharing and allow your Mac account.

  2. 02

    Add your Mac

    Add the Mac’s local IP address or hostname to My Macs in the iPhone app. Sign in with the Mac account allowed to use Screen Sharing.

  3. 03

    Open your Mac

    Optionally save the login in your iPhone’s Keychain, then reconnect from My Macs. The current development connection is for a trusted local network; desktop and input traffic are not encrypted by this app.

GOOD TO KNOW

A few practical details.

Does it work away from home?

Use local addresses or an active private VPN such as Tailscale on both devices. Do not expose Screen Sharing directly to the internet.

Can I use Command and other Mac keys?

Yes. The remote control bar includes Escape, Tab, Shift, Control, Option, and Command alongside the iPhone keyboard. Input uses your Mac’s Screen Sharing login. Input-method and keyboard-layout compatibility are still being tested.

Can I share every display at once?

The direct client shows the combined desktop supplied by Screen Sharing. Choose an individual display when the Mac supplies supported display-layout metadata, or keep All Displays. Selection changes the local view without reconnecting.

Can I connect to Terminal with an SSH key?

Yes. Enable Remote Login on your Mac and choose Terminal in its menu. Create or import an Ed25519 OpenSSH key under Edit Mac → SSH Key, then add the public key to your Mac account’s authorized_keys. Password login is also available. Keys apply to Terminal, not Screen Sharing.

Does it sync with iCloud?

Only if you enable it in App Settings. Sync is off by default and uses iCloud Keychain for saved Mac names, addresses, ports and display/input settings. Privacy depends on your Apple Account, trusted devices and iCloud Keychain security. Passwords, SSH private keys, server trust and saved text are excluded. Turning sync off keeps local Macs and existing cloud copies; cloud-copy removal is separate.

Is this ready for production?

It is a development beta. Faster view changes, physical-device reliability checks, release packaging, and public distribution are still in progress.

What is it built on?

The current standalone client uses LibVNCClient to connect to macOS Screen Sharing. Mac Companion uses GPL-3.0 with applicable dependency licenses and upstream notices. See the license and credits.
